title: Ridgely and Celestin split the Tuxedo band
summary: Barnes explains the break between Ridgely and Celestin over money and how he and others persuaded Celestin to form his own band with Jeanette Sullivan on piano.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh I see, they had fallen out. I want to ask you, Paul, why did Ridgely and Celestad fall out? They just didn't agree about running the band?
Well that's the point I want to come to. In fact what went between those two people, none of us actually never do it, but it was something concerning a few dollars.

But anyway, we thought probably Celestad wasn't getting a right deal, but maybe Ridgely may be in the right, we actually don't know. But before Ridgely died they told me it was just concerning a little money. And it was a terrible mistake that they made because the band was too great. So I took Simon Marrera, John Marrera, and myself and Abbie Foster, Chinese we called him, drum player. We went over to Celestad's house and talked Celestad into making up his own band. And called it Celestad's original Tuxedo band. So Celestad said, well if you all want to be back with me I'll do it. So we formed Celestad's original Tuxedo band. But we couldn't get Emma Barrett, the one that people call the bell girl, we couldn't get her to leave.

She stayed with Ridgely. So we had to get a piano player and in those times lady piano players were very popular with bands in those days. So we went across the lake and we met, I got a girl over there, Jeanette Sullivan, her name is. She got married to Norvin Kimball.
